tagline: Over Towne Pass and down below sea level.
intro: Out of the Panamint Valley the highway goes over Towne Pass, about 4,950 feet up, and comes down into the north end of Death Valley at Stovepipe Wells, less than ten feet above the sea. It runs southeast down the valley to Furnace Creek, near the turnoff for Badwater Basin, and leaves by way of Furnace Creek Wash.

The Death Valley '49ers came in roughly this way, from the east, in late 1849, looking for a short route to the mines. Tourists followed in the 1920s, when Herman Eichbaum opened a toll road to his resort at Stovepipe Wells and charged two dollars a car.

moments.title: Stovepipe Wells
moments.text: Once the only known water on the old Cross-Valley road. When sand buried it, someone set a length of stovepipe in it as a marker, and the name followed.

moments.title: Burnt Wagons
moments.text: Near here the Jayhawker party of '49ers burned their wagons, dried the meat of some of their oxen and went on west on foot.

moments.title: Furnace Creek
moments.text: A village 190 feet below sea level, once called Greenland Ranch for its alfalfa fields, where the thermometer read 134 degrees on July 10, 1913. Some meteorologists still doubt it.

practical: Flash floods close the highway in Furnace Creek Wash, on the way out of the valley to the east, at least once a year.
